gap: No result ChatGPT got states that TESmart's 8-port HDMI KVMs read hotkeys only from the dedicated keyboard/mouse ports, or that TESmart names keyboards that fail on those ports: Logitech MX series, Roccat, Dell KB813-type keyboards with a card slot, and some Microsoft models. TESmart's fix is to move the keyboard to a standard USB port, but hotkey switching stops working there.
standout_why: I read officekithq.com (best 8-port, 5 picks), mamalinux.com (8 best 8-port for home lab, which includes the 'TESmart 8X1' rackmount) and workcocoon.com (8-port guide). They cover EDID, which cables come in the box, USB 2.0 vs 3.0 and cascading. mamalinux says 'IP configuration on Linux requires a Windows application', and officekithq passes on MT-VIKI's 'states support for wireless keyboards'. None of the three says which keyboard port handles hotkeys or names any keyboard the maker excludes. workcocoon names no 8-port product at all. ChatGPT cited none of the results, and its answer says nothing about which keyboards work.
decides: This confirms the TESmart HKS801 line is a sound pick, with a caveat for shoppers who use Logitech MX, Roccat or Dell KB813-style keyboards. Those keyboards may not work on the K/M ports. On the other USB ports they type, but switching then needs the front panel, the IR remote or RS232/LAN on P23/L23. On the M24, the store lists front-panel buttons, hotkeys, mouse wheel double-click and IR remote as switching methods, and separately says it has a LAN port for TCP/IP remote control. Under the same terms, the L23 ($143.99 today) beats the P23 ($399) only when 4K30 is enough. The P23's 4K60 and the M24's VRR / G-Sync / FreeSync are what the extra money buys.

findings.label: Ports that accept hotkeys
findings.value: Only the dedicated keyboard and mouse ports. A keyboard plugged into a USB 2.0/3.0 port types but cannot send hotkeys.
findings.source_title: TESmart Support: The Hotkey Function Does Not Work
findings.note: TESmart's wording: 'The KVM switch is designed to support the hotkey function only on these dedicated ports.' The article recommends the USB 2.0/3.0 ports for keyboards that won't work on the K/M ports.

findings.label: Keyboards TESmart reports as incompatible on the dedicated K/M ports
findings.value: Dell KB813 and similar keyboards with a card slot; Logitech MX series; Roccat; some Microsoft keyboard models
findings.source_title: TESmart Support: The Hotkey Function Does Not Work
findings.note: TESmart's stated cause is proprietary protocols or excessive bandwidth. The article's 'applicable product line' header says Dual/Triple Monitor KVM, but its model list also names single-monitor 8-port units (HKS0801A1U, HKS0801A30).

findings.label: Changing the hotkey trigger
findings.value: Not supported. HKS0801A1U, HKS0801A30, HKS1601A1U and HKS1601A10 are listed as models where the hotkey cannot be changed.
findings.source_title: TESmart Support: The Hotkey Function Does Not Work
findings.note: The link from HKS0801A1U to HKS801-E23 comes from TESmart's support article title 'HKS801-E23 Previously Named HKS0801A1U'. That title appeared in search results; I did not open the article. The E23 shows as unavailable ($309.99) in the TESmart store data.

findings.label: Keyboard types the maker flags for hotkey trouble
findings.value: Wireless, Bluetooth or macro-enabled keyboards, and keyboard software that remaps keys. Standard USB ports 'operate in passthrough mode and do not participate in hotkey detection'.
findings.source_title: How TESmart KVM Hotkeys Work (TESmart blog, 2026-01-16)
findings.note: Maker's own blog post. It names no models.
